metadata.scope: AES-256-GCM encryption-at-rest, wired into app/services/postgres_session_store.py::ChatTurn.content -- the actual text of every stored user query/assistant answer.

sensitive_data_identified.why_sensitive: Raw text of every user query and assistant answer ever sent through the app -- can contain anything a user typed while chatting about their uploaded documents.
Documented as 'populated from the first user turn (truncated)' -- would be sensitive if populated, but no code path that writes it was found in this pass.
sensitive_data_identified.status: NOT ENCRYPTED -- not currently populated by any code path found; out of scope until it's actually used.

NOT ENCRYPTED -- explicitly out of scope for this pass (see app/core/encryption.py's own module docstring): wiring encryption here requires a migration story and touches PyMuPDF/OCR/S3-sync, all of which read the raw file directly.

integration_boundary.write_path: plaintext content (str) -> _encrypt_content() [AES-256-GCM, session_id bound as associated data] -> 'enc1:' + base64(ciphertext) persisted as ChatTurn.content (Text column, no schema change)
integration_boundary.read_path: ChatTurn.content read -> _decrypt_content() [checks 'enc1:' prefix; legacy plaintext rows without it are returned as-is] -> plaintext returned to the application

key_management.mechanism: Settings.encryption_key_b64 (app/core/config.py), loaded from ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64 in backend/.env via pydantic-settings -- the same mechanism every other config value in this app uses.
key_management.real_bug_found_and_fixed_this_pass: app.core.encryption's own _load_key() reads raw os.environ by default, but this codebase's .env is parsed by pydantic-settings and never exported to the process environment -- so a value set only in .env was silently invisible to any caller relying on the os.environ fallback. Fixed by having postgres_session_store.py pass key_b64=settings.encryption_key_b64 explicitly on every call, confirmed by 6 existing DB-backed tests (test_agent_graph_stream.py, test_vision_diagnose.py, test_weather_service.py) that started failing with EncryptionKeyMissingError before this fix and pass cleanly after it.
key_management.never_committed: backend/.env is untracked (confirmed: git log --all -- backend/.env is empty); backend/.env.example documents the variable with an empty placeholder value.

existing_plaintext_record_strategy: BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE READ, NO FORCED MIGRATION: a stored value without the 'enc1:' prefix is treated as a legacy plaintext row and returned as-is by _decrypt_content -- it remains readable without any migration step. Every NEW write is unconditionally encrypted (there is no code path that writes plaintext once a key is configured; if the key is missing, the write fails closed instead of falling back to plaintext). Verified by tests/test_postgres_session_store_encryption.py::TestBackwardCompatibilityWithLegacyPlaintextRows (2 tests).

concrete_demonstration.application_value: What does the document say about [REDACTED SENSITIVE EXAMPLE]?
concrete_demonstration.decrypted_via_normal_read_path: What does the document say about [REDACTED SENSITIVE EXAMPLE]?

measured_results.successful_encrypted_writes: 12/12 test cases exercising append_turn succeeded as expected (including the 1 case that correctly failed closed on a missing key)
measured_results.wrong_key_rejection_rate: 2/2 (100%) -- TestWrongKey and the session-isolation cross-AAD case both correctly raise EncryptionIntegrityError
measured_results.missing_key_fail_closed_rate: 2/2 (100%) -- both write-without-key and read-without-key correctly raise EncryptionKeyMissingError, no plaintext ever persisted or returned

expected_security_outcomes: A database dump/backup of chat_turns.content never exposes chat content in plaintext for any row written after this pass.

A stolen encryption key alone is insufficient to decrypt a different session's content if presented with the wrong session_id as associated data (defense in depth beyond the existing session_id/tenant_id ownership checks).
A tampered or corrupted ciphertext row is detected and raises, never silently returns garbage or partial data.
The application never silently degrades to storing plaintext when the key is missing -- it fails the write/read instead.
remaining_limitations: Only ChatTurn.content is encrypted -- uploaded document files, FAISS index/metadata, and ChatSession.title (currently unpopulated) are not, and are explicitly disclosed as out of scope for this pass.
This is APPLICATION-LEVEL encryption, not PLATFORM-LEVEL (e.g. an encrypted EBS volume) -- see docs/CHECKLIST.md's Encryption row for that distinction, unchanged by this pass.
No key-rotation procedure is implemented -- rotating ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64 would make all previously-encrypted rows undecryptable (a real, disclosed operational gap, not solved here).
This does NOT constitute GDPR/HIPAA compliance by itself -- it is one control among many such a certification would require.
